To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ED is a significant and under treated health problem, which has the potential for improved treatment and prevention through the involvement of community pharmacists.
• ED is common, underdiagnosed and undertreated.
• The prevalence of erectile dysfunction (ED) is increasing, with an estimated 152 million men worldwide affected in 1995, and 322 million expected by 2025.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the pharmacist as a health care provider and the potential for community pharmacies to provide a range of health care services in the future.
the potential role of community pharmacists in improving the treatment and management of ED.

how the pharmacist can be best supported to provide a range of services to meet the needs and expectations of the public in a cost effective manner, and how the profession can be best prepared to respond to these challenges.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ED can be a premonitory sign of serious health problems and a symptom of poor communication in health care services.

ED can be a pre-emptive sign of vascular disease and diabetes, and a sign of poor doctor-patient communication, and that the extension of community pharmacy health care would enable men living with ED access effective medications, appropriate diagnostic services and lifestyle support.
the pharmacist is well placed to improve the care of men with erectile dysfunction, and to improve the treatment of the underlying causes of erectile dysfunction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the pharmacist’s role in improving the management of erectile dysfunction and the underlying causes is to promote and facilitate access to effective and safe medications, to support the adoption of healthier lifestyles, to encourage the timely diagnosis of underlying conditions and to help men with erectile dysfunction to access appropriate and timely care.
we have demonstrated the potential for pharmacists to provide an important contribution to the treatment of erectile dysfuction and its underlying causes.
we need to do more to help men to seek help and to get help.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pharmacist has the opportunity to play a key role in improving the care of men with ED.

the pharmacist's role in addressing ED is a natural extension of the role of pharmacists in promoting healthy lifestyles, in the management of long-term conditions and in providing a range of services in community pharmacies.
the pharmacist's role in the management of ED and its underlying causes is likely to expand.
